images.text: Procuring the right IT product is often a key element in a company's success. However, not taking the time you need to properly negotiate inadvisable vendor contracts is sometimes a faulty business procedure. In order not to face legal pitfalls when dealing with technology contracts, take into consideration the following tips.

Before getting into any negotiation, assess the requirements and goals that your organization has, and define what the project scope, duration, and budget are. By doing so, you can have a bigger picture of the real systems requirements that your organization needs. Not assessing carefully the system requirements to achieve those goals can lead to additional costs. Once you have identified your needs, you can then issue a request for proposals (RFP), which will allow you to evaluate the best technology systems bid that fits your organization's needs. Through an RFP, technology vendors will submit proposals based on your specific needs and capabilities. You also need to make sure not to skimp on due diligence. Analyze each proposal deeply. Not double-checking references, past performances and industry reputation can affect negatively your project. Consider not choosing just one final vendor, but the best two in order to have a better chance to get a more beneficial outcome from the negotiations.

Finally, try not to accept any boilerplate contracts. Quite too often, technology vendor proposals include contracts that are always the same, and focus more on protecting the vendor's interests instead of yours. Demand to have a proposal that is tailored to your company's needs, and make sure the rights and obligations stated in the contract are equally balanced for both parties. If a vendor insists on not changing the contract, it is time to consider other vendors.
